source: run138/RAW_OUTCOMES.json (22 existing ordinarily gradient-trained RNN checkpoints)
question: Do exact learned unit recurrent rays certify exact task output, and can output-gain residuals predict the first finite-horizon counting failure across two architectures and two training precisions?
eligibility: A[j,j] == 1 exactly as stored binary rational; E[plus,j] > 0; E[plus,k] <= 0 and A[k,j] <= 0 for every k != j. All tests use exact Fraction.from_float, no tolerances.
primary_endpoint: For every eligible checkpoint, exact integer first n>=1 with |y(+^n)-n| > 1/10, as n=floor((1/10)/|w[j]*E[plus,j]-1|)+1; independent checker must verify exact minimality and ray induction.
scalar_success: Fraction of eligible checkpoints independently verified to have the exact predicted first failure n; target 1.0, with at least 2 eligible checkpoints per precision and at least 1 from each dimension.
strongest_competitor: This is an elementary identity restricted to known single-coordinate invariant rays, not a generally applicable neural algorithm-acquisition certificate; no inference about mixed-token counting.
cheapest_falsification: Recompute eligibility directly from raw A/E/w and independently check n-1/n via exact Fraction arithmetic; compare counts and groupings.
publishable_threshold: Predictive improvement on prospectively frozen held-out trained architectures and unseen task families, robust to adversarial hidden gates and with a primary-literature novelty audit.
learning_relevance_threshold: Must use gradient-trained A,E,w checkpoints (not constructed coefficients), matched float32/float64 and 2D/3D, and demonstrate a diagnostic consequence not visible from 256-step pass/fail alone.
kill_condition: Any independent verification mismatch kills the exact law as implemented; if no precision/architecture coverage or no measurable horizon separation, kill the empirical extension and keep only the elementary theorem.
wildcard: On one preselected eligible checkpoint, perturb output readout by one adjacent floating-point representable step; assess first-failure horizon change; do not alter main evaluation.
claims_scope: Only repeated increment input, mathematical real-arithmetic recurrence with stored binary coefficients, and strict absolute error > 0.1; not float32 runtime, not arbitrary input words.
compute: CPU only; no retraining or user hardware
